<USER_REQUEST>
IMPLEMENT AND VERIFY THE COMPLETE PRODUCTION-SAFE FIX FOR THE
AUTOMATED INCREMENTAL SATELLITE MONITORING WORKFLOW.

============================================================
CONTEXT
============================================================

We are developing the TN Forest / Environmental Monitoring System.

The system uses:

Frontend:
- React + TypeScript

Backend:
- Node.js + Express + TypeScript
- Layered architecture:
  Routes → Controllers → Services → Repositories → Models

Database:
- MongoDB + Mongoose

Satellite:
- REAL Google Earth Engine (GEE)
- Sentinel-2 optical
- Sentinel-1 SAR

Processing:
- Real GeoTIFF
- Local raster processing
- CRS/resolution validation
- NDVI / NDWI / NDBI
- Change Detection
- Evidence Fusion
- Alerts

IMPORTANT:
Production execution MUST use authentic GEE imagery.

DO NOT introduce:
- fake satellite IDs
- fake image dates
- deterministic mock catalog entries
- simulated GEE responses
- simulated Drive files
- fake processing results
- fake change detections
- fake observations

============================================================
CURRENT REAL MANUAL-TEST STATE
============================================================

Zone:

Name:
sathiyar

Zone ID:
ZONE-260906-7064

Zone is:
PROTECTED / PERMANENT

Active optical baseline:

Sensor:
SENTINEL_2

Baseline image:
COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED/20200109T051201_20200109T051844_T43PHM

Baseline acquisition:
2020-01-09T05:25:54.755Z

Baseline:
ACTIVE
isActive = true

No SAR baseline is currently established.

Current Monitoring UI before fix:

Active Monitoring Areas = 1
Observations Discovered = 0
Processed Pipeline = 0
Alerts Generated = 0
Pipeline Health = 100% OK

Area:
sathiyar
Type = PERMANENT
Last Processed Sensing Date = —
Latest Observation = Pending scan
Status = PENDING

When:

Monitoring Jobs
    →
Run Incremental Scan

the system reported:

Cycle completed in 12539ms.
Discovered: 0
Processed: 0
Alerts: 0

============================================================
CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE
============================================================

The diagnostic investigation has confirmed that the problem is a CODE BUG.

Real GEE discovery is working.

For the Sathiyar polygon, real GEE returns approximately 33 valid
Sentinel-2 observations under the configured cloud threshold.

Example:

Candidate #1:
COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED/20200109T051201_20200109T051844_T43PHM

Acquisition:
2020-01-09T05:25:54.755Z

This is the ACTIVE BASELINE.

Candidate #2:

COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED/20200114T051149_20200114T052300_T43PHM

Acquisition:
2020-01-14T05:25:54.659Z

This is a valid newer observation.

Candidate #3:

COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED/20200124T051109_20200124T052518_T43PHM

Acquisition:
2020-01-24T05:25:53.472Z

This is also a valid newer observation.

There are additional newer real observations, including observations
around 2020-09-01.

The system currently fails because:

1. Baseline start timestamp is truncated to YYYY-MM-DD.

Example:

2020-01-09T05:25:55.755Z

becomes:

2020-01-09

GEE therefore includes the baseline image.

2. Candidate filtering occurs too late.

3. Candidate #1 is correctly rejected because it is the baseline.

4. The rejection throws an exception.

5. processAreaIncremental() does not isolate errors per observation.

6. The exception aborts the entire candidate loop.

7. Candidate #2 and all later valid observations are never reached.

8. The outer cycle reports:

Discovered: 0
Processed: 0
Alerts: 0

This behavior is incorrect.

============================================================
FILES IDENTIFIED DURING INVESTIGATION
============================================================

Primary files:

server/src/services/AutomatedMonitoringService.ts

server/src/services/gee/GeeSatelliteService.ts

Also inspect all directly related files/classes for:
- MonitoringSchedulerService
- MonitoringSchedulerWorker
- MonitoringJob
- IncrementalMonitoringRecord
- SatelliteMetadata
- Baseline
- ChangeDetection
- satellite repository
- monitoring repository
- GEE provider/client
- frontend monitoring service
- frontend Monitoring Jobs page

Do not modify unrelated modules.

============================================================
OFFICIAL INCREMENTAL MONITORING POLICY
============================================================

IMPLEMENT:

OPTION A — LATEST OBSERVATION ONLY

This is now the official production behavior.

The incremental monitoring system MUST NOT process every historical
observation between the baseline and the present.

Instead:

1. Find all REAL eligible satellite observations newer than the active
   baseline / last processed observation.

2. Apply all eligibility filters.

3. Select ONLY THE NEWEST ELIGIBLE OBSERVATION.

4. Process/export/download/process ONLY that newest observation.

5. Do NOT process older eligible observations in the same incremental cycle.

Example:

Baseline:
2020-01-09

GEE returns:

2020-01-09  ← baseline → REJECT
2020-01-14  ← eligible
2020-01-24  ← eligible
2020-02-03  ← eligible
2020-03-01  ← eligible
...
2020-09-01  ← newest eligible

The incremental scan MUST select:

2020-09-01

and process ONLY that observation.

It MUST NOT process:

2020-01-14
2020-01-24
2020-02-03
etc.

============================================================
IMPORTANT: LATEST OBSERVATION DOES NOT MEAN LATEST IMAGE BLINDLY
============================================================

The newest GEE image must first pass ALL eligibility checks.

Selection order must conceptually be:

REAL GEE OBSERVATIONS
        ↓
Sensor filter
        ↓
Geometry/intersection filter
        ↓
Cloud filter
        ↓
Acquisition date > active baseline
        ↓
Acquisition date > last processed observation, if one exists
        ↓
Exclude baseline image ID
        ↓
Exclude completed/duplicate observation
        ↓
Sort by acquisition timestamp DESC
        ↓
SELECT NEWEST ELIGIBLE OBSERVATION
        ↓
Process ONLY this observation

Do NOT simply select the newest raw GEE image before filtering.

============================================================
FIX 1 — PRE-FILTER BEFORE PIPELINE PROCESSING
============================================================

In:

AutomatedMonitoringService

ensure all candidates are filtered BEFORE calling:

processObservationPipeline()

Reject an observation if:

1. observation.imageId === activeBaseline.imageId

OR

2. observation.acquisitionDate <= activeBaseline.acquisitionDate

OR

3. lastProcessedSensingDate exists AND
   observation.acquisitionDate <= lastProcessedSensingDate

OR

4. observation has already been successfully processed according to
   IncrementalMonitoringRecord / existing processing state

OR

5. sensor/source does not match the active sensor track

OR

6. geometry/intersection validation fails

OR

7. cloud threshold fails

The baseline must never enter the actual current-image processing
pipeline.

Keep the defensive baseline safety check inside
processObservationPipeline() as a second safety layer.

============================================================
FIX 2 — TIMESTAMP PRECISION
============================================================

Current problem:

startDate.toISOString().slice(0, 10)

removes the time component.

Do NOT depend on this for correctness.

Use exact timestamps wherever supported by the GEE API.

If GEE listImages requires date-only boundaries, it is acceptable to
query the calendar date containing the baseline PROVIDED that the
application strictly pre-filters candidates using the actual timestamps:

candidate.acquisitionDate > activeBaseline.acquisitionDate

and:

candidate.imageId !== activeBaseline.imageId

Therefore the baseline image must never be processed.

Do NOT compare only dates when determining temporal precedence.

Use full timestamps.

============================================================
FIX 3 — FIRST SCAN WHEN lastProcessedSensingDate IS NULL
============================================================

A newly activated zone can have:

lastProcessedSensingDate = null

This is valid.

For the FIRST incremental scan:

lower temporal boundary =
activeBaseline.acquisitionDate

Then:

candidate.acquisitionDate > activeBaseline.acquisitionDate

After finding eligible candidates:

SELECT ONLY THE NEWEST ELIGIBLE OBSERVATION.

After that observation is successfully processed, update the
incremental state so that:

lastProcessedSensingDate =
successful current observation acquisition timestamp

Do NOT leave it permanently NULL after successful processing.

============================================================
FIX 4 — SECOND AND FUTURE SCANS
============================================================

After the first successful scan:

lastProcessedSensingDate = <latest successfully processed timestamp>

Future scans must search for observations newer than:

lastProcessedSensingDate

Example:

Baseline:
2020-01-09

First scan:
Latest eligible = 2020-09-01

After successful processing:

lastProcessedSensingDate =
2020-09-01

Next scan:

Only observations where:

acquisitionDate > 2020-09-01

are eligible.

If there is no newer observation:

return a successful "no new observation" result.

Example:

Raw GEE candidates:
5

Eligible after filters:
0

Selected:
none

Result:

Discovered: 0
Processed: 0
Alerts: 0
Status: WAITING_FOR_NEW_OBSERVATION

This is an EXPECTED result when there genuinely is no newer
observation.

Do not treat it as a system error.

============================================================
FIX 5 — ONE BAD CANDIDATE MUST NOT ABORT THE SCAN
============================================================

Never allow one candidate failure to terminate processing/discovery of
the entire cycle.

However, because we are implementing LATEST OBSERVATION ONLY:

The system should first determine the newest eligible candidate.

Then process ONLY that candidate.

If that selected newest candidate fails processing:

- record the failure
- do not silently claim success
- do not process a random older candidate automatically
- return an appropriate failure/retry state

Do NOT fall back to an older image unless the existing architecture
explicitly defines a retry/fallback policy.

For discovery diagnostics, one rejected candidate must never abort
candidate evaluation.

============================================================
FIX 6 — DISCOVERY COUNTS
============================================================

Make count semantics explicit.

Internally maintain:

rawCandidatesCount
baselineRejectedCount
temporalRejectedCount
duplicateRejectedCount
cloudRejectedCount
geometryRejectedCount
sensorRejectedCount
eligibleCandidatesCount
selectedCandidate
processedCount
failedCount
alertsGenerated

For the UI DTO:

"Observations Discovered" should represent the number of genuinely
eligible NEW observations according to the established DTO semantics.

Do not report:

Discovered: 0

simply because the first raw candidate was the baseline.

Example:

Raw GEE candidates = 33
Baseline rejected = 1
Eligible = 32
Selected newest = 1
Processed = 1

The scan should clearly expose these numbers in diagnostics.

============================================================
FIX 7 — LATEST OBSERVATION SELECTION
============================================================

After filtering:

eligibleCandidates.sort(
  acquisitionDate DESC
)

selectedCandidate = eligibleCandidates[0]

Process ONLY:

selectedCandidate

Do not loop through all eligible candidates for processing.

The monitoring cycle must not generate 32 exports/Drive files/change
detections for one scan.

Exactly one newest eligible current observation should be processed
per incremental scan.

============================================================
FIX 8 — REAL GEE DISCOVERY
============================================================

The on-demand:

Run Incremental Scan

must continue using real GEE discovery.

Current path:

POST /api/monitoring/run-cycle

→ MonitoringController.runMonitoringCycle

→ MonitoringSchedulerService.runAutomatedMonitoringCycle()

→ AutomatedMonitoringService.runAutomatedMonitoringCycle()

→ processAreaIncremental()

→ discoverNewObservations()

→ GeeSatelliteService

→ GeeSatelliteProvider

→ GeeClientService

→ real GEE REST API

Preserve this architecture.

Do not replace GEE discovery with MongoDB-only discovery for the
on-demand incremental scan.

============================================================
FIX 9 — MONITORING WORKER VS ON-DEMAND SCAN
============================================================

There are two monitoring paths.

PATH A:

Run Incremental Scan button

Uses real GEE discovery.

PATH B:

MonitoringSchedulerWorker hourly daemon

Currently uses SatelliteMetadata records from MongoDB in its local
processing path.

Do not incorrectly merge these two architectures.

However, both paths must obey the same fundamental rules:

- active baseline required
- real observations only
- baseline cannot be current observation
- observation must be newer than baseline
- observation must be newer than last processed timestamp
- duplicates must not be processed
- latest-observation-only policy must be respected
- baseline remains immutable

If the scheduled worker is intended to initiate discovery itself,
ensure it eventually uses the same correct discovery semantics rather
than assuming MongoDB already contains the current image.

Do not make unrelated architectural changes.

============================================================
FIX 10 — SATELLITE CATALOG VS MONITORING
============================================================

The Satellite Catalog and Monitoring system serve different purposes.

Satellite Catalog:
- discovers/indexes satellite metadata
- may contain multiple candidate images
- does not automatically mean those images have been processed

Monitoring:
- finds the newest eligible observation
- processes that observation
- creates/updates incremental monitoring state
- hands the processed observation to Change Detection

Do not assume that a catalog record automatically means a current
observation has been processed.

Do not fabricate a catalog record to satisfy monitoring.

============================================================
FIX 11 — SAR PROVIDER BUG
============================================================

There is a confirmed provider dispatch issue.

In:

server/src/services/gee/GeeSatelliteService.ts

when:

sensor === SensorType.SAR

the code must call:

searchSarImages()

and NOT:

searchOpticalImages()

Required mapping:

OPTICAL
→ Sentinel-2
→ searchOpticalImages()

SAR
→ Sentinel-1
→ searchSarImages()

Do not query Sentinel-2 twice when SAR is requested.

============================================================
FIX 12 — SENSOR TRACK ISOLATION
============================================================

Active baseline:

SENTINEL_2 / OPTICAL

Therefore the current manual test should process:

OPTICAL / Sentinel-2

Do not use Sentinel-1 as a substitute for the optical baseline.

If a SAR baseline is not established:

do not perform optical-vs-SAR pixel change detection.

Keep optical and SAR tracks separate.

Maximum:

1 active optical baseline per zone
1 active SAR baseline per zone

============================================================
FIX 13 — ACTIVE BASELINE IMMUTABILITY
============================================================

During incremental monitoring:

DO NOT:

- replace the active baseline
- change the baseline image ID
- change baseline acquisition date
- automatically activate current observation as baseline
- retire baseline automatically
- create a new baseline automatically

The active baseline remains fixed.

Monitoring only creates/processes CURRENT OBSERVATIONS.

============================================================
FIX 14 — CHANGE DETECTION HANDOFF
============================================================

The correct production sequence is:

ACTIVE BASELINE
        ↓
MONITORING INCREMENTAL SCAN
        ↓
REAL NEWEST ELIGIBLE GEE OBSERVATION
        ↓
GEE EXPORT
        ↓
GOOGLE DRIVE
        ↓
LOCAL GEOTIFF
        ↓
RASTER VALIDATION
        ↓
CRS / RESOLUTION VALIDATION
        ↓
SPECTRAL PROCESSING
        ↓
CURRENT OBSERVATION READY
        ↓
CHANGE DETECTION
        ↓
BASELINE vs CURRENT
        ↓
CHANGE RESULT
        ↓
ALERT IF THRESHOLD CROSSED

Do not create a ChangeDetection record before a real current
observation is successfully acquired/processed.

Do not bypass the monitoring pipeline by manually creating fake
current observations.

============================================================
FIX 15 — CHANGE DETECTION INPUTS
============================================================

Change Detection must compare:

ACTIVE BASELINE
+
NEW CURRENT OBSERVATION

It must NOT compare:

baseline vs baseline

or:

current vs current

or:

two arbitrary catalog records

or:

unprocessed metadata-only records.

Before pixel-level comparison validate:

- same CRS
- same width
- same height
- same resolution
- spatial alignment
- valid raster
- compatible bands

If reprojection/resampling is required, use the existing
RasterHarmonizationService rather than silently comparing incompatible
rasters.

============================================================
FIX 16 — LAST PROCESSED STATE
============================================================

Use the existing:

IncrementalMonitoringRecord

and/or equivalent monitoring state.

After successful current-observation processing, store:

- zone/area ID
- current observation image ID
- acquisition timestamp
- processing status
- job ID
- relevant metadata
- completed timestamp

Update:

lastProcessedSensingDate

ONLY after successful processing.

Do not update lastProcessedSensingDate when processing fails.

This prevents a failed observation from being permanently skipped.

============================================================
FIX 17 — IDEMPOTENCY
============================================================

The same current observation must not be processed twice.

Use the existing job/observation locking mechanism.

A previously completed observation should be skipped.

Example:

First scan:

2020-09-01
→ PROCESS
→ SUCCESS
→ lastProcessedSensingDate = 2020-09-01

Second scan:

2020-09-01
→ DUPLICATE
→ SKIP

No duplicate processing.

No duplicate Drive export.

No duplicate ChangeDetection event.

No duplicate alert caused solely by repeated scanning.

============================================================
FIX 18 — NO AUTO-BASELINE ADVANCEMENT
============================================================

After processing:

Baseline:
2020-01-09

Current:
2020-09-01

DO NOT change baseline to 2020-09-01.

Instead:

Baseline remains:
2020-01-09

Current observation:
2020-09-01

ChangeDetection:
Baseline vs Current

If a future administrative workflow wants to promote a current image
to a new baseline, that must happen through explicit baseline
activation and safety validation.

============================================================
FIX 19 — CLOUD FILTERING
============================================================

Preserve the configured cloud threshold.

For Sentinel-2 currently:

max cloud cover = 20%

A candidate is eligible only if:

cloud <= configured threshold

Do not hardcode fake cloud values.

Use real GEE metadata.

============================================================
FIX 20 — GEOMETRY FILTERING
============================================================

The candidate must genuinely intersect the monitored zone geometry.

Use the existing GeoJSON polygon.

Do not create a candidate simply because the image exists somewhere
in the world.

Candidate must cover/intersect the monitored zone.

============================================================
FIX 21 — MONITORING JOB STATE MACHINE
============================================================

Inspect the existing MonitoringJob status enum/state machine.

Ensure the lifecycle is logically consistent.

Example:

PENDING
   ↓
RUNNING / PROCESSING
   ↓
DISCOVERY
   ↓
CURRENT_OBSERVATION_SELECTED
   ↓
PROCESSING
   ↓
COMPLETED

If no newer observation exists:

PENDING/RUNNING
   ↓
WAITING_FOR_NEW_OBSERVATION

If processing fails:

PROCESSING
   ↓
FAILED

Do not report COMPLETED when processing failed.

Do not report:

Discovered = 0

if the scan actually discovered eligible observations but processing
failed.

Separate:

discovery success

from:

processing success.

============================================================
FIX 22 — ERROR SEMANTICS
============================================================

Distinguish:

NO_NEW_OBSERVATION

from:

GEE_API_ERROR

from:

EXPORT_FAILED

from:

DRIVE_FILE_MISSING

from:

RASTER_INVALID

from:

PROCESSING_FAILED

from:

DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE

from:

AUTHENTICATION_ERROR

A real "no new image" condition is not a system failure.

A GEE API failure must not be represented as:

0 observations

without an error indicator.

A MongoDB connection failure must never be interpreted as:

0 active zones.

============================================================
FIX 23 — DATABASE CONNECTION SAFETY
============================================================

If MongoDB is disconnected:

return/throw:

DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE

HTTP 503 where appropriate.

Do NOT silently return:

[]

or:

0 active monitoring areas.

This prevents database outages from appearing as a healthy empty
monitoring system.

============================================================
FIX 24 — DIAGNOSTIC LOGGING
============================================================

For each incremental scan log:

============================================================
INCREMENTAL MONITORING CYCLE
============================================================

ZONE:
<zone>

ZONE ID:
<id>

ACTIVE BASELINE:
<image ID>

BASELINE ACQUISITION:
<timestamp>

SENSOR:
<sensor>

LAST PROCESSED:
<timestamp or NULL>

SEARCH WINDOW:
<start timestamp>
→
<end timestamp>

RAW GEE CANDIDATES:
<number>

FILTER RESULTS:

Baseline rejected:
<number>

Temporal rejected:
<number>

Duplicate rejected:
<number>

Cloud rejected:
<number>

Geometry rejected:
<number>

Sensor rejected:
<number>

Eligible candidates:
<number>

SELECTED LATEST OBSERVATION:
<image ID>

ACQUISITION:
<timestamp>

CLOUD:
<value>

PROCESSING:
STARTED / SUCCESS / FAILED

LAST PROCESSED SENSING DATE:
<value>

CHANGE DETECTION:
READY / NOT READY

ALERTS:
<number>

FINAL STATUS:
<status>

Do not log:
- access tokens
- refresh tokens
- passwords
- credentials
- secrets

============================================================
FIX 25 — CANDIDATE DIAGNOSTIC DETAIL
============================================================

For debugging, log each candidate decision.

Example:

Candidate:
COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED/20200109...

Acquisition:
2020-01-09T05:25:54.755Z

Cloud:
2.038%

Geometry:
PASS

Sensor:
PASS

Temporal:
FAIL

Baseline ID:
MATCH

Final:
REJECT

Reason:
ACTIVE_BASELINE_IMAGE

Then:

Candidate:
COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED/20200114...

Temporal:
PASS

Duplicate:
PASS

Final:
ELIGIBLE

Do this for discovery diagnostics.

============================================================
FIX 26 — FIRST REAL MANUAL TEST
============================================================

After implementation, run ONE REAL incremental monitoring cycle for:

sathiyar

Active baseline:

COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED/20200109T051201_20200109T051844_T43PHM

The real GEE search is known to return multiple observations.

The system must:

1. Discover real GEE candidates.
2. Reject the baseline.
3. Continue evaluating other candidates.
4. Filter all invalid candidates.
5. Select the NEWEST eligible observation.
6. Process ONLY that observation.
7. Update incremental state after successful processing.
8. Leave the active baseline unchanged.
9. Make the current observation available for Change Detection.

============================================================
EXPECTED FIRST-SCAN BEHAVIOR
============================================================

Example:

Raw GEE candidates:
33

Baseline candidate:
1

Eligible candidates:
32

Newest eligible:
<latest real Sentinel-2 image returned by GEE>

Selected:
1

Processed:
1

Older eligible candidates:
NOT PROCESSED

Active baseline:
UNCHANGED

lastProcessedSensingDate:
<selected observation acquisition timestamp>

============================================================
IMPORTANT ABOUT THE 2020-09-01 CATALOG RECORD
============================================================

The earlier diagnostic initially observed a Satellite Catalog record
dated approximately 2020-09-01.

However, the database inspection also showed that after the clean reset
there was only the baseline SatelliteMetadata record, while live GEE
returned the larger set of real observations.

Therefore:

DO NOT assume the 2020-09-01 record is still present in MongoDB.

Use REAL GEE discovery as the source of truth for the incremental
on-demand scan.

If a catalog record exists, it may be used as metadata, but it must
not prevent real GEE discovery.

============================================================
FIX 27 — CURRENT OBSERVATION EXPORT
============================================================

Once the newest eligible observation is selected:

Run the existing real export pipeline:

GEE
→ image:export
→ real GEE task ID
→ poll task
→ Google Drive
→ Drive file ID
→ download
→ local GeoTIFF
→ raster validation
→ CRS/resolution
→ spectral processing

Do not create a fake current image.

Do not mark the current observation PROCESSED before the actual
pipeline succeeds.

============================================================
FIX 28 — GOOGLE DRIVE
============================================================

Use the existing real Google Drive integration.

Verify:

- real Drive file ID
- file exists
- file size > 0
- local download succeeds

Do not simulate Drive delivery.

============================================================
FIX 29 — RASTER VALIDATION
============================================================

Current observation must pass:

- file exists
- file size > 0
- width > 0
- height > 0
- band count valid
- CRS detected
- metric-safe CRS or correct harmonization
- resolution validated
- spectral indices calculated where applicable

Do not mark current observation processed before these checks.

============================================================
FIX 30 — AREA CALCULATION SAFETY
============================================================

When Change Detection eventually runs:

Use actual metric pixel area.

For example:

pixelAreaM2 =
resolutionX × resolutionY

changedAreaM2 =
changedPixels × pixelAreaM2

changedAreaHa =
changedAreaM2 / 10000

affectedAreaPercentage =
changedPixels / validPixels × 100

Do not derive percentage from rounded hectare values.

Keep:

affectedAreaPercentage

separate from:

evidenceScore.

============================================================
FIX 31 — NO CHANGE DETECTION BYPASS
============================================================

Do not modify Change Detection merely to hide the monitoring problem.

Fix Monitoring first.

Only when a valid current observation exists should:

Change Detection

be executed.

Correct chain:

Monitoring
→ current observation
→ Change Detection

============================================================
REGRESSION TESTS REQUIRED
============================================================

Add/update tests for ALL of the following:

1. Active baseline returned by GEE is rejected.

2. Baseline rejection does not abort candidate discovery.

3. Candidate #2 is still evaluated after Candidate #1 is rejected.

4. Candidate newer than baseline is accepted.

5. Candidate older than baseline is rejected.

6. Candidate exactly equal to baseline timestamp is rejected.

7. Candidate with matching baseline image ID is rejected.

8. lastProcessedSensingDate = NULL works.

9. Candidate equal to lastProcessedSensingDate is rejected.

10. Candidate older than lastProcessedSensingDate is rejected.

11. Candidate newer than lastProcessedSensingDate is eligible.

12. Duplicate completed observation is rejected.

13. Newest eligible observation is selected.

14. Older eligible observations are NOT processed.

15. Only ONE current observation is processed per incremental cycle.

16. Successful processing updates lastProcessedSensingDate.

17. Failed processing does NOT update lastProcessedSensingDate.

18. Second scan does not reprocess the same observation.

19. No newer observation returns WAITING_FOR_NEW_OBSERVATION.

20. GEE API failure returns GEE_API_ERROR rather than empty success.

21. Database disconnect returns DATABASE_UNAVAILABLE.

22. Cloud filtering works.

23. Geometry filtering works.

24. Optical sensor uses Sentinel-2 provider.

25. SAR sensor uses Sentinel-1 provider.

26. Optical and SAR tracks remain isolated.

27. Active baseline remains unchanged after monitoring.

28. No automatic baseline advancement occurs.

29. No fake GEE observations exist.

30. Real GEE asset IDs are preserved.

31. Current observation cannot equal baseline.

32. Current raster must be genuinely exported/downloaded.

33. Current raster validation must succeed before PROCESSED.

34. Change Detection cannot run without a valid current observation.

35. Change Detection receives baseline + current observation.

36. Duplicate ChangeDetection event is prevented for same
    baseline/current pair.

37. Duplicate alerts are prevented where applicable.

38. Latest-observation-only policy is enforced.

============================================================
FRONTEND REQUIREMENTS
============================================================

Do not redesign the UI unnecessarily.

Keep:

Run Incremental Scan

Refresh

Recover Stale Jobs

Create Monitoring Job

But make the displayed information accurate.

After a successful scan, the UI should show:

Observations Discovered:
<number of eligible observations>

Processed Pipeline:
1

Latest Observation:
<real image date>

Status:
COMPLETED / READY

Last Processed Sensing Date:
<real timestamp>

If there is no newer image:

Observations Discovered:
0

Processed Pipeline:
0

Latest Observation:
No new observation

Status:
WAITING_FOR_NEW_OBSERVATION

This should not appear as an error.

If GEE fails:

Status:
GEE ERROR

not:

healthy 0 observations.

============================================================
MONITORING JOB UI SEMANTICS
============================================================

Ensure the UI distinguishes:

JOB CREATED

from:

JOB RUNNING

from:

DISCOVERING

from:

CURRENT OBSERVATION SELECTED

from:

PROCESSING

from:

COMPLETED

from:

WAITING_FOR_NEW_OBSERVATION

from:

FAILED

Do not show "Completed" simply because the API request itself
returned HTTP 200.

The actual job processing state must be reflected.

============================================================
CHANGE DETECTION UI SEMANTICS
============================================================

Before current observation exists:

Change Detection page may show:

"No current observation available.
Run Incremental Monitoring first."

After current observation exists:

Show:

Baseline:
<date>

Current Observation:
